children: Sweden's central bank kept its key policy interest rate unchanged at 1.75% as expected on Thursday but said the policy rate should be raised more going forward than had been projected in its June forecast.
"If the outlook for inflation and economic activity remains unchanged, it is expected that the increases to the policy rate will begin this year," the Riksbank said in a statement.
Analysts in a Reuters poll had been unanimous in seeing no change this time.
The Riksbank has been growing increasingly worried about the chance inflation will pick up after higher-than-expected readings during the summer.
Conflict in the Middle East has pushed the price of oil to around $100 a barrel and a resolution looks distant.
The crown currency has been hit by a growing rate gap with European Central Bank, which is expected to hike again before the end of the year.
"If there were to be signs of a larger and more persistent upturn in inflation, the Riksbank would raise the policy rate at a faster pace than in the current forecast," the central bank said.
Price pressures, however, are currently muted making the country an outlier in Europe and giving rate-setters in Sweden some breathing room before they need to tighten policy.
Norway's central bank will announce its policy decision later in the day with a small majority expecting a hike to 4.50%.
